value.name: Pulse train
value.responsibility: Computes a traffic mark's pulse train once for every painter: its legs, glow layers, gradient stops and each leg's motion
value.description: pulse_train(&TrafficMark) answers the train as plain data with public fields: the core, span, repeats, cycle, stops, four glow layers and the legs, each with its bar and its motion, steady or turning. It follows the SVG painter's math operation for operation, so SVG bytes stay identical. pulse_slide(&LegMotion, seconds) maps a moment to a leg's position: the painter owns the clock and the scene answers where a pulse is at that moment (ADR 0071). pulse_breadth(line_width) and turn_distance(lengths) answer the two pulse numbers Painting needs. The constants, the leg cutting and the former traffic functions stay private.

value.name: Codex connection
value.responsibility: Opens one Codex child's connection, its epoch, identity authorities and transport, and opens sessions on it
value.description: TASK-653.11, ./connection. openCodexConnection({ child, recordPrefix }) returns a plain-data CodexConnection (child, epoch, identity, transport) with no function-valued member: a fresh child and epoch from the record prefix, the authorities that name identities in them, and the transport over the child's stdio. A child that already exited yields a closed transport, so the host registers its dynamic dispatchers after open and only while the transport is open, and no namespace TypeError is thrown. openCodexSession(connection, options) returns { session, control }; the caller owns the control, which delivers the transport's notifications and server requests to the session and disposes of it. One connection belongs to one child and one epoch; the process that yields the children stays apart (ADR 0089).

value.label: the transport over the child's stdio

value.name: Codex failures
value.responsibility: Reads what went wrong in Codex from a thrown value, and makes the error Codex would throw for a failure a caller states
value.description: TASK-653.11, ./failure. readCodexFailure(error) returns a CodexFailure: a mutation with its method and outcome, a refused write, a remote error with its method and JSON-RPC code, a process failure with its code and whether it is terminal, an executable failure or an identity refusal with its code, each with the error's message; anything else is null. It reads only the value it is given and walks no cause or aggregate member: a mutation failure is caused by a transport error, so a walk would change answers. createCodexFailure(spec, cause?) makes the error for the mutation, process, refused-write and remote kinds with the message the spec states, and reads back as its spec. The seven error classes that callers tested with instanceof are private and keep their names and messages (ADR 0089).

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk#ttPYQNXo
changes.value: Seven names (ADR 0085): Stage::new(theme, size, Pace), present(Presentation), arrive(Painting, Arrival), depart(Departure), draw(Surface, now) -> Motion and pick. The pace, a move's phases and the longest step of the clock, comes at birth. A presentation states only what changed: each value it states replaces the last, and a value it leaves out stays. An arrival is a cut, a carry, an entrance or a flight into a card; a departure is a leaving, a stay, a clear or the end of a flight into a card, so the page states each decision once and in no required order within a turn. The stage owns its clock. Each timed value carries its own moment (the camera, the awaited step, the light, a sweep, an entrance, a flight into a card and a leaving), and the stage reads the clock once for each such moment and once for each frame, so a stepped clock records it frame by frame. A cut, a carry, a stay, a clear and a sweep with no lines name no moment and read nothing. Each draw says whether to keep a strip canvas's parts: Surface::Strips wraps the canvas in the stage's part store and culls to the stage's size, and Surface::Direct draws whole, as the GPU canvas, a recording canvas and a counting canvas need. A frame answers its Motion: still, traffic alone or moving.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/9ncuT5DP#9diqPrFw
changes.value: TASK-653.11: createCodexProcess is the owner itself; the wrapper in process.ts is gone, and the owner's options let tests replace the spawn, the file system and the clock. Its failures are read through readCodexFailure as kind process, with their code and whether they are terminal. The host names the storage. Archboard names one Archboard-only CODEX_HOME and SQLite home under the state directory, which serve every server on the machine, so one sign-in serves them all; each server keeps its own owner lock and epoch ledger under its port. Its config.toml gets the auto-review defaults it lacks (approvals_reviewer auto_review, workspace-write sandbox with network access) and keeps whatever Codex or a person set; a config naming another SQLite home, or not TOML, is refused. The child runs in the coordinator's directory under the server's state directory, which is no checkout and holds no vault, only a link to the server's archboard skill: the coordinator thread works there, so a command it runs without -C is refused, while each workhorse thread works in its own checkout. The child's environment is a short allow-list plus what the host adds. Archboard adds the server's own URL, with auto-start off, and the server's bin directory first on PATH: a thread's archboard is the server's own source in whichever checkout the thread works in, and it never starts another server. On shutdown, stdin closes first. The owner waits within a short EOF grace, then reaps every remaining group within the composed deadline. A release's native Codex binary gets the variables that Codex's own launcher would set.

changes.value: Owns every duration and the waiting around them: named waits, pauses and deadlines, and one getter for durations that something other than a wait takes as a number

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/vKEsyHFk#sZ4chHDX
changes.value: Callers do not write the waiting themselves (ADR: timing owns the waiting, and one getter reads the rest). It exports nine names. waitUntil polls a probe on a named wait whose private policy keeps its bound, its cadence, whether it sleeps first, where it checks the bound, whether the bound's own moment counts and how its last sleep meets the bound. A caller may pass its own bound, an outer cap, a signal and a clock, and gets the value found or a refusal with its reason and the bound in seconds, which the caller puts in its own sentence. pause sleeps one named cadence for a loop that keeps its own decisions across passes. deadline ends a named duration from a moment, never past an optional cap; an age check compares the time now with it, and the caller keeps its own operator. durationMs is the one keyed getter, for what takes a number and is not a wait: a stylesheet, a physics constant, a timer, a library option or a message. No wait bound or cadence is readable through it except the model lock's poll, which a synchronous loop sleeps with Bun.sleepSync. painterPhasesJson, reachHopDelayMs, columnSlideSettledMs, codexRestartDelayMs and localityDefaultSinceSeconds keep their computations. The Clock port (now, and after(ms, run) that returns a cancel) is the seam a caller or a test passes; the default clock stays private and reads Date.now and setTimeout when called. A duration is named "<owner>.<key>" over the owner groups, which stay inside with what each pulls against. The names and policies have a published half, the Codex groups and processGroup that @archboard/codex-realtime-voice bundles, and a host half that a build under the published condition leaves out, where a host name throws by name. It stays browser-safe: no process and no node: imports.

changes.value: TASK-653.11: createCodexTransport is private; openCodexConnection opens it over the child's stdio with the connection's identity authority. It writes each frame through encodeFrame and turns a refusal into its write error (a usage error for a value with no JSON form, else frame-too-large). replaceIdentity, its dead call and the ?? fallbacks are gone from CodexTransport (owner decision 22). Its error classes stay inside, under their names and messages, and callers read them through readCodexFailure.
